Comedian Ari Shaffir returns to Joe Rogan for episode 2492. Shaffir is known for dark tales and a wandering life. His storytelling shows mix shock with strange warmth.

Rogan lets him loose on travel, drugs, and comic lore. Each story tests how far a joke can go. The pair share years of common friends and rooms. The episode is raunchy and free by design. It suits fans of raw stand-up talk who want two veterans swapping the kind of tales they never tell on stage. Chaos and charm mix in his usual measure.
podcast-tuckercarlson-8SWoEGXk-V8:
Former congressman Curt Weldon represented Pennsylvania for twenty years and has argued ever since that the official story of September 11 is incomplete. With Tucker Carlson, he says it is time to finally tell the truth about 9/11, drawing on his own knowledge of intelligence failures before the attacks.

Weldon was a senior voice on defense in the House, and his claims carry the weight of a man who sat in the briefings. Carlson gives him the floor for the full account: warnings ignored, programs shut down, questions never answered. Historians and the 9/11 Commission reached different conclusions, and listeners should weigh Weldon's version against that record. The episode preserves a former insider's dissent, which is valuable whatever verdict a listener reaches.
